lit.'<p>Al tirar de la caja, el <b>roce está:
'

As you pull the box, static friction grows just like the applied force and the box does not move, up to a maximum of μₛ·N. Beyond that value the box slides and kinetic friction μ_k·N, a little smaller, takes over: that is why it is harder to start motion than to keep it going. Friction depends on the surfaces (μ) and on the normal force.

'
lit.'<p>Cuando la fuerza neta no es cero el:
'

When the net force is not zero the body accelerates: Fnet = m·a. Here the net force is the applied force minus kinetic friction. With the same net force, a box with twice the mass has half the acceleration. 1 N is the force that gives 1 kg an acceleration of 1 m/s².

'
lit.'<p>Dos carros se empujan con un resorte:
'

Two carts push apart with a compressed spring. Cart A pushes B and B pushes A with an equal and opposite force (third law). The forces are equal, but the lighter cart gets more acceleration and leaves faster: m₁·v₁ = m₂·v₂. Action and reaction never cancel because they act on different bodies.

'
lit.'<p>La <b>masa</b> (kg) mide la cantidad:
'

Mass (kg) measures the amount of matter and the inertia; weight is the gravitational force: W = m·g. A 5 kg body weighs 49 N on Earth (g = 9.8 m/s²), 8.1 N on the Moon and 124 N on Jupiter. The spring balance measures weight: it stretches more where gravity is stronger.

'
lit.'<p>Un resorte ejerce una <b>fuerza elás:
'

A spring exerts an elastic force proportional to its deformation: F = k·x, where k is the spring constant (N/m). Hanging more mass stretches the spring in proportion: the F–x graph is a straight line of slope k. A stiffer spring (larger k) stretches less with the same load.

'
lit.'<p>Una <b>fuerza</b> es una interacción:
'

A force is an interaction between two bodies and is measured in newtons (N). Two forces act on the box: its weight (the Earth pulls it down) and the normal force (the table pushes it up). They are equal and opposite: the net force is zero and the box stays at rest. That is Newton’s first law (inertia).

'
